findings.description: Research filenames do not distinguish map boundaries. For map `eval`, `.chart-eval-*.dispatch` also matches dispatches for map `eval-workers`. The report glob in op_handoff has the same ambiguity.
findings.failure_mode: Five dispatches for `eval-workers` prevent `eval` from dispatching research. Handing off `eval` also inlines `eval-workers` reports into its priority-1 planning context.
findings.suggested_fix: Store reports and dispatch markers in per-map directories, or record map ownership explicitly and filter by exact ownership.

findings.description: Comparing porcelain status strings does not verify that the main tree stayed unchanged. Further edits to an already-modified file retain the same status entry; writes inside an already-ignored directory can also retain the same directory entry.
findings.failure_mode: A probe can overwrite existing operator edits or modify ignored runtime state while this helper exits 0 and reports that the main tree was unchanged.
findings.suggested_fix: Compare file contents and path membership before and after, including dirty files and individual ignored files, or enforce filesystem isolation that prevents main-tree writes.

findings.description: The research scope check compares newly appearing status entries rather than file contents. If an application file was already modified before research-begin, overwriting it produces the same entry and is accepted. The additional timestamp checks cover only .run and .beads.
findings.failure_mode: The Write-capable researcher can change an already-dirty application file and still pass research-end, violating its enforced single-report write scope and potentially destroying operator work.
findings.suggested_fix: Enforce an exact report-path allowlist on Write calls, and verify content hashes and path membership outside that report rather than comparing status entries.

findings.description: Map slugs and ticket slugs both match SLUG_RE ('^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,47}$'), so hyphens appear in both halves of the file names `chart-<slug>-<ticket>.md` and `.chart-<slug>-<ticket>.dispatch`. The per-map globs are therefore ambiguous: op_research_begin counts `.chart-${SLUG}-*.dispatch` (line 444) and op_handoff inlines `${RESEARCH}/chart-${SLUG}-*.md` (line 379). For map `eval` the glob `chart-eval-*.md` also matches every report of map `eval-workers`; for map `eval-workers` it matches map `eval`'s ticket `workers-foo`.
findings.failure_mode: (1) research-begin on map `eval` is refused with 'already dispatched N research subagents (cap 5)' when a sibling map `eval-workers` used the slots, so a legitimate dispatch exits 1. (2) op_handoff writes another map's research reports into `grimoires/loa/context/chart-eval.md`, which /plan-and-analyze ingests as priority-1 'settled' context for the wrong PRD.
findings.suggested_fix: Use an unambiguous separator between map slug and ticket slug (e.g. `chart-<slug>__<ticket>.md`, or a per-map subdirectory `research/<slug>/<ticket>.md`), or record the map slug inside the marker/report and filter on that instead of a glob. Apply the same rule in chart-researcher.md, chart.md and the SKILL/REFERENCE docs.

findings.cross_file_justification: chart-researcher.md grants an unrestricted Write tool and promises 'Write exactly one file: the report path'; the only mechanical enforcement is op_research_end in chart-ticket.sh.
findings.description: The scope check in op_research_end drops every status entry whose path starts with `grimoires/loa/research/` (awk filter at line 458). A prompt-injected or misbehaving subagent can therefore overwrite any other ticket's report, any other map's report, or the `.chart-*.dispatch` marker files, and the check still passes. op_handoff later inlines those reports into the hand-off snapshot.
findings.failure_mode: Research output for ticket A silently replaces the already-reviewed report for ticket B (or a report on a different map); research-end exits 0 and the contaminated report reaches `grimoires/loa/context/chart-<slug>.md` as priority-1 context. Overwriting the marker also resets its mtime, blinding the `find -newer` check for .run/.beads.
findings.suggested_fix: Exempt only the exact expected report path (`grimoires/loa/research/chart-${SLUG}-${TICKET}.md`) from `bad`, not the whole directory, and treat any change to `.chart-*.dispatch` files as a failure. Consider storing the marker outside the research dir (e.g. under .run/ or mktemp) so the subagent's Write tool cannot reach it.

findings.description:
section_append passes operator free text via `awk -v line="$2"`. POSIX/gawk process escape sequences in -v assignments, and san1 strips control characters but not backslashes. A decision line containing `
`, `	`, `\` or a Windows path (`C:
ew	ree`) is rewritten: `
` becomes a literal newline, unknown escapes like `\d` are collapsed to `d` with a warning on stderr.
findings.failure_mode: The 'Decisions so far' / 'Out of scope' bullet is split across lines or its text altered in the tracked map doc; section_bullets and the `grep -qF "(${row}, "` idempotency check then misparse it, and a map validator expecting one `- name (DEC-..., bead): text` line per decision fails.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass the text through the environment instead: `LINE="$2" SEC="## $1" awk 'BEGIN{line=ENVIRON["LINE"]; sec=ENVIRON["SEC"]} ...'`. Same for `set_status` for consistency.

findings.description: map_rows merges pending ledger files from `${SCRIPT_DIR}/../../grimoires/loa/a2a/*/decisions-pending.yaml`, i.e. the live repository, even when `--root DIR` points at a fixture tree. The map doc, research dir and context dir honour ROOT but the pending-row lookup does not.
findings.failure_mode: Tests or fixture runs with --root pick up live worktree pending rows (or miss fixture pending rows), so row_for_source/bead_row return rows from the wrong tree; op_close may reject live pending rows while operating on a fixture map.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `"${G}/a2a/"*/decisions-pending.yaml` (G is derived from ROOT) so the lookup follows --root like every other path in the script.

findings.cross_file_justification: Both files are in the diff and must agree on the br JSON schema; they currently do not.
findings.description: get-ready-work.sh excludes decision tickets with `(.issue_type // "") != "question"` only, while chart-frontier.sh selects them with `(.issue_type // .type // "")`. Similarly create-sprint-task.sh accepts labels as strings or `{name}` objects, but chart-frontier.sh does `.labels[] | tostring | startswith("decision:")`, which never matches an object label. The three scripts assume different br output shapes.
findings.failure_mode: On a br release that emits `type` instead of `issue_type`, question beads pass through get-ready-work.sh into /implement and /run work selection, defeating the header's 'dropped whatever labels they carry' guarantee. On a release that emits object labels, chart-frontier.sh returns an empty frontier for every map.
findings.suggested_fix: Factor one jq helper for 'type of bead' and 'label names' (string or {name}) and use it in get-ready-work.sh, chart-frontier.sh, chart-ticket.sh and create-sprint-task.sh; add a bats case for each shape.

findings.description: The new priority-1 entry `grimoires/loa/context/chart-*.md` and the Phase 0 rule ('Other snapshots are not ingested') sit next to the unchanged priority-2 glob `grimoires/loa/context/*.md`, which also matches every `chart-<slug>.md` snapshot. Phase 0 still says 'Reads all files from grimoires/loa/context/'.
findings.failure_mode: With two or more handed-off maps, the non-chosen snapshot is still loaded as priority-2 user context, so its 'settled, do not re-ask' decisions leak into the PRD the operator explicitly said does not consume that map.
findings.suggested_fix: Exclude `chart-*.md` from the priority-2 context glob (or move snapshots to a dedicated directory such as `grimoires/loa/context/maps/`), and make the Phase 0 bullet say that only the chosen snapshot is read.

findings.description: The main-tree verdict is a string compare of `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all --ignored=matching` before and after. That is blind to (a) further edits to tracked files that were already modified before the probe (status line unchanged), (b) new files inside a directory that is already ignored as a whole (`--ignored=matching` lists the directory, not its contents), and (c) edits to already-untracked files. chart-ticket.sh research-end adds a `find -newer` check for .run/.beads; the probe does not.
findings.failure_mode: A probe that writes into the operator's dirty working file or into `.run/`/`.beads/` of the main tree exits 0 and the unblock ticket is treated as clean, contrary to 'exits 1 when the main tree's status changed'.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a content fingerprint alongside the status snapshot, e.g. `git -C $MAIN diff | sha256sum` plus `git -C $MAIN ls-files -o --exclude-standard -z | xargs -0 sha256sum`, and a `find $MAIN -newer <marker> -not -path '*/.git/*'` pass like research-end.

findings.description: The FR-1.1 override for `git branch -D spike/<slug>` reads `grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml` from the working tree and trusts a row whose transition `by` starts with `operator:`. The agent this hook constrains has a Write tool and can author that row directly (bypassing dec-write-lib's interactive check), then delete the unmerged spike branch.
findings.failure_mode: An agent (or injected instruction) appends a forged `status: decided` row with `by: operator:x` and `source: grimoires/loa/spikes/<slug>.md`, after which the hook lets `git branch -D spike/<slug>` through and the unmerged prototype is lost.
findings.suggested_fix: Read the ledger from a committed ref (`git show HEAD:grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml`) rather than the worktree, and/or require the spike branch to be pushed (`git rev-parse -q --verify refs/remotes/origin/spike/<slug>` with the same tip) before allowing the force delete, since the design says the spike is 'pushed, never merged'.

findings.description: SP-1 is documented as a fence with listed misses (show/apply, switch -c, worktree add, SHAs). Several equally short forms are not listed and not matched: `git fetch origin spike/x && git merge FETCH_HEAD`, `git reset --hard spike/x` / `git branch -f feature spike/x` / `git read-tree -u spike/x` (all make another branch carry spike content), `git checkout -p spike/x` (n=1 so _sp1_checkout_copies passes), `gh pr create --head "$(git branch --show-current)"` on a spike branch (the --head regex is satisfied so the on-branch check is skipped), and `gh api repos/:o/:r/pulls -f head=spike/x`.
findings.failure_mode: Spike content enters a working branch or a PR is opened from a spike branch without the hook firing, while the message to the agent claims these are 'never merged ... or opened as a PR'.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `reset|read-tree|branch -f|branch --force` to the merge-family alternation, treat `checkout -p/--patch <spike ref>` as a copy, drop the `! _match(--head)` short-circuit when the head value is not a literal ref (fall through to the on-branch check), and extend the documented 'Misses' list for the rest so run-mode-ice.sh can cover them.

findings.description: op_close appends `## Closed` with a raw `>>` into the tracked map doc, while every other doc write goes through mktemp + mv. It also skips the append entirely when a `## Closed` header already exists, so a map abandoned once and later closed with --consumed-by records neither the new date nor the new reason.
findings.failure_mode: A failure mid-append (disk full, signal) leaves a half-written map doc that set_status then rewrites; a re-close after a prior close silently loses the consumed-by cycle id, which /plan-and-analyze cites as the hand-off provenance.
findings.suggested_fix: Route the `## Closed` line through section_append (creating the section via a temp-file swap when missing) and always append a dated bullet, letting the Status line carry the final state.
